verdict.rationale: Superpowers is driven by conversation. Its skills auto-trigger from plain requests ("Fix this bug" routes to systematic-debugging), the brainstorming skill draws a spec out of dialogue, and implementation starts once the user says "go"; community users report simply telling it to go. Slash commands are available but not required. Missing for 10: deterministic intent routing (the docs say it only "should" default into planning), and natural-language parsing that comes from the product itself rather than the host agent.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can operate the product with natural-language commands

citations.quote: "Fix this bug" → superpowers:systematic-debugging first, then domain skills.
because the skills trigger automatically, you don't need to do anything special. Your coding agent just has Superpowers.
once you say "go", it launches a *subagent-driven-development* process, having agents work through each engineering task
Once it's teased a spec out of the conversation, it shows it to you in chunks short enough to actually read and digest.
It does a quick, clear task right away, agrees a small change with you in chat, and writes a design document for a project. You can override its call
